# Background {#sec-background}

 The Running Back(RB) is a vital part of an offense and can leave a big impact on a game based on their performance. "Running Backs are a dynamic element in the offense, capable of rushing with the ball, receiving passes, and providing pass protection. They must exhibit a blend of speed, agility, and toughness to consistently gain yards on the ground or catch passes out of the backfield." (Nisay,2024) With RB having to do so much it is only natural to assume that some RB are better than others and that every RB has something they accede at more than their peers. When we look at RB or any other position for that matter in a way that we are only focusing on what they do good in we can start to put these positions into subgroups. These subgroups can help us characterize these players or to get a general understanding of how they play. 
 Why is it important to know what a players subgroups is when it comes to football? Understanding and knowing a players subgroup can be useful for the team itself to know how to properly utilize the player that they have at their disposal and get the most out of them, or a team might look at the opposing teams player position subgroups and use those subgroups to help form a plan that could lead them to a victory. In fantasy football knowing a players subgroup could be good to evaluate how your player will get most of their points and it can be good for finding out whether the team that the player plays against are good at stopping the given player. So, the subgroups of a position can be a key element in a teams game plan and a fantasy managers game plan for a given match. 

## The Research {#sec-TheResearch}

 The question I will be aiming to find is how many definable subgroups do RB's have and what are they? By definable I mean subgroups that do not have cross overs into other subgroups.
 I hypothesize that there are going to be 4 definable subgroups for RB's. I think there will only be 4 not because I think there is only 4 but because I feel there will be a lot of overlap if you make more and more subgroups, and my whole point is to find distinct, definable subgroups. I also believe there will only be 4 subgroups because when you look at other skilled positions on the field there is always at least 4 definable subgroups, so, why would there not be 4 subgroups for RB's.
